newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest power mixed on mild temp, natgas jump.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest power mixed on mild temp, natgas jump.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. were mixed Wednesday versus Tuesday's levels amid mild weather and a rally in natural gas prices, market sources said.
Physical power prices in the upper portion of the Midwest were flat to lower because of moderate power demand, while those in the southern part rose on higher natural gas prices.

In the East Central Area Coordination Agreement (ECAR) district, peak, non-firm electricity prices for Thursday's delivery were discussed at $15.75-$16.75 a megawatt hour (MWh), lower than Tuesday's $16.00-$18.50 range.
Off-peak, non-firm ECAR power for Thursday was quoted near $12.50-$13.50, compared with Tuesday's $12.00-$13.50 for Wednesday delivery.
"Everyone is at the same level because of the cooler weather. There're more sellers than buyers," said an ECAR trader.

He added the surge in Thursday power prices due to reduced output at the 1,100 megawatt (MW) Peach Bottom 2 nuclear unit in Delta, Pa., at the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool did not carry over to ECAR. "It's too far away," he said.
Peak, non-firm power prices in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) for Thursday were assessed at $16.00-$17.50 a MWh, down from Tuesday's next-day quote of $17.50-$18.50.
Off-peak, non-firm MAIN electricity for Thursday was discussed near $11.50, compared with $11.00-$12.50.
In northern MAIN, peak, non-firm power prices were quoted today near $14.00 and off-peak, non-firm values near $7.75.
Peak, non-firm power prices for Thursday delivery in the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) were talked near $15.00 a MWh, compared with Tuesday's range of $15.00-$15.50.
Off-peak, non-firm MAPP electricity was pegged at $8.00-$10.50, compared with $8.00-$9.00 on Tuesday.
There has been little spot MAPP activity because of the ongoing transmission contraints in the region, Midwest traders said.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in the southern part of $18.00-$19.00 a MWh, a tighter range than Tuesday's $17.00-$19.00.
